title: Excitonic Stripe Order in the Two-Orbital Hubbard-Kanamori Model
authors: Rafael D. Soares, Luke Staszewski, Chunhan Feng, Alexander Wietek
abstract: Excitonic condensation and stripe formation are two distinct manifestations of electronic correlations. While excitonic order naturally arises in multi-orbital systems, stripe order is a prominent feature of doped correlated-electron models. Here, we investigate an excitonic analogue of stripe order in the two--orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model on the square lattice, characterized by a spatial modulation of inter-orbital particle-hole coherence and, in the orbital-parity-symmetric limit, spontaneous breaking of a relative orbital $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. Using unrestricted real-space Hartree-Fock calculations complemented by random-phase-approximation instability analysis, we determine how the Kanamori interactions select different excitonic channels. The sign of Hund's exchange controls the spin character of the condensate: ferromagnetic Hund coupling favors triplet excitonic order, whereas antiferromagnetic Hund coupling stabilizes singlet excitonic order. Upon doping, commensurate excitonic density waves develop incommensurate textures, including excitonic stripes and, in the triplet sector, spiral excitonic density waves. We further show that crystal-field splitting strongly reorganizes the excitonic instability by modifying inter-orbital nesting and can stabilize triplet excitonic order even in the absence of pair hopping. Our results establish excitonic stripes as a distinct symmetry-broken state of multi-orbital correlated systems and identify microscopic routes for their stabilization.
summary: This work explores excitonic stripe order in the two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model, treating it as an excitonic analogue of charge/spin stripes. Using Hartree-Fock and RPA, the authors demonstrate that excitonic stripes form a distinct symmetry-broken state whose spin character depends critically on the Hund's coupling sign. The results provide a detailed phase diagram mapping out various correlated electronic phases.
main_problem: The paper investigates excitonic stripe order, an excitonic analogue of stripe order, in a multi-orbital correlated electron system.
main_result: Excitonic stripes are established as a distinct symmetry-broken state in multi-orbital correlated systems, with the spin character (singlet vs. triplet) dictated by the sign of Hund's exchange coupling.
method: The study employs unrestricted real-space Hartree-Fock calculations complemented by Random-Phase-Approximation (RPA) instability analysis to map out phase diagrams.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model on a square lattice. The Hamiltonian includes hopping, crystal-field splitting, and various repulsive/exchange interactions.
key_observables: Excitonic order, stripe order (spatial modulation of inter-orbital particle-hole coherence), and the spontaneous breaking of a relative orbital Z2 symmetry.
important_parameters: Hund's exchange coupling (J_H), crystal-field splitting (Delta_cf), and doping level are key parameters controlling the resulting ordered phase.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations (Hartree-Fock) and RPA, which are noted to be limited by the Mermin-Wagner theorem for true long-range order at finite temperature.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates principal ordered phases (Néel, orbital density wave, excitonic order) at the Hartree-Fock level. Figure 2 shows temperature-electron density phase diagrams for various regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the internal symmetries of the Hamiltonian, develops gap equations for different ordered phases (AFM, Triplet Excitonic, ODW, Singlet Excitonic), and uses RPA susceptibility calculations to determine instability boundaries.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the study's rigorous use of symmetry analysis and mean-field techniques for identifying distinct symmetry-broken phases is relevant to understanding order parameters in complex quantum many-body systems.
